attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, in his own voice.

semantics.note: 'We will eventually see' is an unhedged forecast. The 'probably' in the preceding sentence qualifies the claim that smarter AI is needed, not the arrival itself. The grandchildren qualifier is kept. Context suggests arrival depends on new research, but he stated no formal antecedent.

contract.note: The plain reading of coherent prose search answers and dependable everyday organising help is ordinary and fair. Requiring both parts, and allowing contradiction only by proof of impossibility, matches an open-ended 'eventually'. The ambiguity about reliability is flagged properly.

evidence.note: Independent Pew measurement from 2025 shows deployed search AI summaries of paragraph length. This supports the search part only and does not grade writing quality or reliability.
Google's own announcement of an organising agent. It shows the feature is advertised and available, not that it performs dependably.

Dated benchmark showing everyday task successes but inconsistent repeat performance (31% of tasks that passed once failed on another try). It does not establish dependable life organisation, and present failures cannot contradict an open-ended forecast.

reviews.rationale: Open-ended forecast with two parts. The search part is supported by e1. Dependable agents that can organise lives are not established: e2 is only an advertisement and e3 shows inconsistent performance. The early-resolution rule needs both parts, so it is not met. Nothing shows the capability is impossible. Unresolved.
